analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date and adds documentation (head lines 627-629) for the opt-in ModelCheckpointConversationLiveTests. The documentation now says the report records delta files and greedy output tokens, and it mentions the env var DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS=0 as a complete-file baseline. No source, crypto, auth, or runtime behavior changes in this diff, so no security control regresses.

Relevant threat T-041 (prefix cache, SSD tier, AT-REST artifacts, TTL/purge). The docs mention an 'incremental checkpoints' / delta-file concept. If the corresponding source change (not in the supplied batch) introduces a new on-disk delta artifact format, it might need threat-model review: HMAC-only naming, AAD metadata with no prompt-derived data, TTL/LRU sweep coverage, and write-endurance accounting. T-041's detection_hint lists SSDBlockStore metadata/AAD, name derivation and purge points as review triggers. That is an unverified contract here, not evidence of regression.

Minor note: the test report records 'greedy output tokens' for a synthetic test. The same doc states that token-level diagnostics must stay in explicitly owned local evidence and never go to telemetry. The test uses an isolated ephemeral cache and fixed public prompts, so no concern from the docs alone. Also verified: the test command uses env -i with a limited variable set and never uses production cache roots/keys (documented in the surrounding text).

Next pass: if the paired source PR adds incremental/delta checkpoint files, confirm delta files use the same K_lookup HMAC names, AES-GCM AAD, salt scoping, TTL/sweep, and disk-budget/ledger accounting as complete files, and that no raw prefix hashes or token IDs reach disk.
